title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Reference + Day‑2 Ops, Upgrades, and Customer Requirements
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments covering VPC and on‑prem reference architectures, packaging and distribution guidance, day‑2 operations (monitoring, backups, scaling), and a prescriptive upgrade + rollback procedure. It also contains a customer requirements library mapping common customer constraints to configuration patterns we support and recommended SLAs. Intended audience: Solutions Engineers, Platform Engineers, SREs, and Customer Success engineers supporting Private (VPC / on‑prem) rollouts.

Scope
- Reference topologies for typical customer network and compute footprints (small, medium, enterprise).
- Packaging and deployment artifacts for on‑prem installers and VPC manifests.
- Day‑2 operational runbooks: monitoring, alerting, backups, capacity changes.
- Step‑by‑step upgrade procedure with prechecks and automated rollback steps.
- Customer requirements library: mapping regulatory/network/ops requirements to configuration templates.

1) Reference Architectures

1.1 High Level Topology (VPC)
- Control plane: Redwood-managed (optional private control plane available per contract).
- Data plane: customer VPC in a dedicated subnet with private routing to GPU nodes.
- Components: load balancer (internal), inference pool (GPU autoscaling group), caching layer (Redis/managed), metrics & logs forwarder, KMS integration for keys.
- Networking: NAT gateways for egress, VPC endpoints for S3/Blob, security groups with least privilege for inter-service ports (gRPC 9090, HTTP 8080, metrics 9092).

1.2 On‑Prem Reference (co-located in customer DC)
- Hardware: per rack GPU fleet (N ≥ 2), redundant management nodes, local NFS for model artifacts (or air-gapped artifact server).
- Orchestration: RKE2 / EKS-D / vanilla Kubernetes (supported). Helm charts provided for control plane components.
- Connectivity: optional transit gateway to customer cloud; for air‑gapped deployments provide secure portable artifact bundle and offline key provisioning instructions.

1.3 Deployment Profiles
- Small (PoC): 2 GPU nodes, 1 management node, single Redis, non-redundant; recommended for test and evaluation.
- Medium (SMB): 4–8 GPU nodes, 2 management nodes, HA Redis, metrics retention 30d.
- Enterprise: ≥16 GPU nodes, multi‑rack, HA control plane, dedicated logging cluster, cross‑region failover via model replication.

2) Packaging & Distribution

- Delivery formats: Helm chart + OCI images (recommended), TAR bundle for air‑gapped installers, and an Ansible playbook for initial bootstrap.
- Artifact signing: All packages are signed with Redwood release keys; customers validate signatures with provided public key.
- KMS/HSM: Integrations supported with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and PKCS#11 HSM devices. Step to provision keys are in the appendix.

3) Pre‑Deployment Checklist (must be completed before on‑site / VPC rollout)

| Item | Purpose | Owner | Required | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|----------|-------|
| Network CIDR allocation | Avoid IP conflicts | Customer netops | yes | Provide /24 for management, /22 for inference pool |
| Gateway & egress rules | Allow Redwood control plane (if used) | Customer netops | conditional | List of IP ranges provided in order form |
| Storage sizing (models) | Model cache sizing | Customer infra | yes | Estimate: model_size * concurrency * 2 |
| KMS key access | Encrypt keys at rest | Customer security | yes | Provide key ARN or HSM provisioning guide |
| GPU hardware validation | Verify drivers & CUDA | Customer infra | yes | See supported GPUs matrix in appendix |

4) Day‑2 Operations

4.1 Monitoring & Alerts (recommended stack)
- Metrics: Prometheus (node exporter, nvidia-smi exporter), token latency and per-route QPS, cache hit rates.
- Logs: Fluentd/Fluent-bit forward to customer's ELK/Datadog or Redwood remote ingest (contracted).
- Core SLOs to monitor: P95 latency < configured SLO (e.g., 150ms), error rate < 0.1%, token throughput per GPU.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - GPU memory usage > 90% for 5m -> page oncall
  - Model load failure -> P1
  - High cache miss rate (> 30% of requests) -> investigate prefix cache eviction

4.2 Backup & Restore
- Backups: periodic snapshots of model artifacts (if stored on NFS) and control plane etcd backups (for k8s). Frequency: daily incremental, weekly full.
- Restore test: perform restore drill quarterly; document RTO (target 2hr for control plane, 4hr for model replication).

4.3 Scaling & Capacity Changes
- Horizontal scale: add GPU nodes to the autoscaling group / k8s nodepool. Recommended warmup: pre-pull model artifacts using prefetch job to avoid cold starts.
- Vertical scaling: unsupported for GPU instances; prefer horizontal scale-out.

5) Upgrade Procedure (standardized, validated path)

Preconditions (run before any upgrade):
1. Confirm current health: all pods running, error rate < 0.1%, P95 latency within SLO.
2. Create full backups: etcd snapshot + model artifact archive.
3. Notify customer stakeholders and schedule maintenance window (if required).
4. Ensure Canary namespace exists and sample traffic can be routed.

Step‑by‑step upgrade (recommended automated steps):
1. Bump chart version in Helm repo and publish release tag.
2. Deploy to Canary namespace (10% of traffic) with feature flag:enable-new-runtime.
3. Run validation test suite (smoke + 10% of regression prompt set) — pass threshold: no >1% degradation in quality metrics and latency within +20% of baseline.
4. If validation passes, proceed with progressive rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% (each step with 20–30 minute observation window).
5. Monitor for critical alerts; if any P1 triggered, invoke rollback procedure (below).

Rollback procedure (automated playbook):
1. Trigger Helm rollback to previous release (helm rollback <release> 1).
2. Re-route traffic to previously healthy revision via service routing policy.
3. Run smoke tests and confirm health metrics recovered.
4. Collect logs and create a postmortem if degradation was customer impacting.

Emergency rollback (if automated path fails):
- Stop ingest at the load balancer (route to maintenance page) and scale up previous stable nodes with model artifacts imported from backup. Contact Redwood SRE for assisted recovery.

6) Customer Requirements Library (common asks -> config mapping)

| Customer Requirement | Typical Constraint | Redwood Configuration / Pattern | Notes |
|----------------------|--------------------|---------------------------------|-------|
| Air‑gapped deployment | No outbound internet | TAR bundle + offline key provisioning | Provide signed artifacts on USB or secure transfer |
| FIPS / HSM required | Crypto compliance | PKCS#11 HSM + validated agents | Requires additional contract for HSM integrations |
| Strict data residency | Models/data cannot leave region | Deploy control plane in customer VPC/private control plane | Use regional S3/Blob endpoints |
| High availability across AZs | Zero single AZ dependency | Multi-AZ node pools + cross-AZ LB | Ensure model sync meets replication RPO |
| Custom model packaging | Customer provides models | Add to model registry via signed manifest | Validate model format and tokenizer compatibility |

7) Ownership, Runbooks & Contacts
- Ownership: Private Deployments team (eng-private-deployments) owns packaging, charts, and upgrade tooling. Oncall: Eng‑SRE supports infra incidents; Solutions Eng supports customer pre/post deploy.
- Runbooks: See related runbook doc for incident playbooks: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/private-deployments-runbook-2026-03-10
- Escalation matrix: Tier1 (customer ops) -> Tier2 (Solutions Eng) -> Tier3 (Platform/SRE) -> Exec oncall. Contact list stored in PagerDuty integration.

8) FAQs & Known Limitations
- Q: Can customers perform one‑click upgrades?
  A: We provide an automated Helm/Ansible path; one‑click in the Console is available for Dedicated customers under SLA.
- Q: Is model quantization performed during deployment?
  A: Quantized model variants must be provided or we can run offline quantization during onboarding (additional service).

Appendix A: Supported GPUs & Drivers (summary)
- NVIDIA A10, A40, A100 (driver CUDA 12.x recommended). See full matrix in packaging appendix.

Appendix B: Sample CLI commands
- Create etcd snapshot: kubectl -n kube-system exec etcd-0 -- etcdctl snapshot save /backup/etcd-$(date +%F).db
- Helm canary install: helm upgrade --install ri-control ./charts/control --namespace canary --set featureFlags.enableNewRuntime=true --dry-run=false

Appendix C: Troubleshooting checklist (top 5)
1. Model fails to load: check disk permissions and model path, validate model signature.
2. High P95 latency: check batching configuration and KV cache hit ratio.
3. Frequent OOMs: reduce per‑node concurrency or scale nodes.
4. Certificate errors to control plane: validate cert chain and CA rotation status.
5. Slow artifact pulls: ensure registry egress bandwidth and CDN prefetching enabled.
